findings.title: Context secret declaration cannot be reconstructed from the allowed immutable base fields
findings.observed: Step context accepts secretRef carrying referenceId only; valid examples use vault://studio/protected-page-password. Global secretRef and secret defaults are refused, but a step secretRef is accepted. Classifier context collection handles variableRef and text, not secretRef. Revision authoring captures that opaque referenceId; inputs have only nonsecret value hashes; revision configuration has no variables; references.secrets is populated from materialized configuration references and has no alias-to-secretId mapping.
findings.implication: For this accepted context shape, a base-only {referenceId, kind:secretRef, secretId} declaration is not recoverable. T0 explicitly requires STOP/report. A missing entry is not evidence that the reference was unused or equivalent to a token.
findings.requiredCorrection: Aria must rule one canonical declaration identity and its immutable persistence, or close the unsupported context shape explicitly. Prefer extending an existing JSON snapshot only if contract/semantics are ruled; no new column or current-draft lookup by assumption. Test two identical authoring shapes with changed declaration mapping and verify historical base resolution independently of live variables.
findings.owner: Aria ruling; C-int contract; dev persistence; Dara schema only if newly ruled

findings.title: Token-only plain reference hashes are absent from existing base snapshots
findings.observed: AuthoringRevisionIdentity collects global and step context VariableReference/default variable references, but never parses step text. A <var name> token is accepted and materialized by the classifier. Publication stores reference names, not plain values or value hashes, in references; the V12 trigger copies the incomplete authoring_revision_inputs unchanged.
findings.implication: The ruled stepInputHash reads valueHash from nonsecretReferencedValues for text and context references; that value is missing for token-only references. A value change can be missed or base recomputation cannot run. Revision configuration_revision alone must not force all such edits to k=1 in place of the ruled per-step behavior.
findings.requiredCorrection: Extend the one pure reference collector/identity producer to cover canonical text tokens plus allowed context/default/global references before new revisions are published. Persist complete hashes at first publication. Existing immutable rows with missing values need an explicit clean-data/refusal policy; do not synthesize historical hashes from current draft variables.
findings.owner: dev authoring + publication; Aria legacy/base policy; C-int if JSON shape changes

findings.title: One immutable materialization cannot currently accommodate prefix-first execution followed by suffix SOURCE_PLAN
findings.observed: Materialization is one row per session. Its authored_inputs, authored_inputs_hash, context identity and source/config revision are immutable; only live/materialization_revision can change. freeze refuses any existing action or materialization. Current SOURCE_PLAN chooses source references before bootstrap/freeze. Publication and secret lineage assume the single materialization.
findings.implication: After model-free prefix actions, existing bootstrap/freeze cannot install newly selected suffix inputs. Updating the old materialization would violate V14 and invalidate prefix proofs/secret joins. The proposed V21 does not address this.
findings.requiredCorrection: Before DDL installation, choose either a bounded complete pre-prefix materialization whose stable inputs suffice for all future source selections, or a separately ruled append/versioned input design with proof/secret/publication joins bound to each version. A complete source-span universe must respect 200-input/size bounds; do not claim it is free. Any required new tables/constraints/functions go in forward V21, never edited V14/V17.
findings.owner: Aria data-flow decision; dev GuidedMaterializationService/translation; Dara forward schema

findings.title: State-only model fence and current continuation routing do not maintain a model-free prefix
findings.observed: admit writes ACTING and completeStep writes OBSERVING/FINALIZING; completeStep does not accept REPLAYING_PREFIX. reserveModel updates counters/progress without requiring a model-attempt INSERT, so the SQL trigger alone cannot prove zero counters. runnable includes the state; coordinator chooses only plans/dependency-admissions/proposals. Runner ACTIVE excludes it.
findings.implication: Untouched paths either reject prefix work, leave the fence mid-prefix, attempt model planning, or lose ownership. Merely filtering the state out of runnable leaves no durable continuation driver.
findings.requiredCorrection: Specify an atomic durable replay mode/checkpoint, retain state=REPLAYING_PREFIX across ordinary prefix subactions or enforce mode independently, gate both reservation entrypoints, and route restartable prefix work. A new continuation value is not logically mandatory if state plus durable checkpoint is authoritative; however, recommended explicit REPLAY_PREFIX requires V21 replacing the V14 continuation CHECK and coordinator support. Resolve this choice before V21 is installed. Test direct reserveModel, both gateways, restart, heartbeat, cancel, expiry and drift exit.
findings.owner: Aria lifecycle; C-int vocabulary; dev state/runner; Dara continuation CHECK if selected

findings.title: Suffix consumer changes contradict byte-identical reused producer snapshots
findings.observed: The ruled learnedStepHash includes produced binding definitions minus session-bound fields. Binding consumers include consumer step coordinate, slot and destination origin; publication builds this from all exercised edges. Those semantic consumer fields are not in the ruled deny-list.
findings.implication: Editing/deleting/reordering a suffix consumer changes an unchanged prefix producer hash even when its operation/value production is identical. Copying the base hash fails verifier recomputation or the V15 reuse guard; copying stale consumers fails exact-plan validation.
findings.requiredCorrection: Aria must revise the canonical ownership of binding content: commit producer-local identity in producer snapshot and consumer edges at their consumer steps, or another explicit composition with vectors. Keep the complete merged dependency graph and admission provenance independently verified; do not disable the V15 same-hash guard.
findings.owner: Aria hash ruling; C-int vectors; dev hasher/verifier

findings.title: Prefix input and binding identity import is not implemented
findings.observed: Input IDs are freshly randomized during resolve; binding IDs are randomized for a new session allocation. The learned operation and operationHash commit input/binding references. Tables scope IDs by session, so cross-session reuse is structurally possible, but current methods expose no authenticated import path.
findings.implication: Preserving only admission-ID exclusion does not guarantee unchanged learnedStepHash; a re-materialized prefix operation with a different sourceInputId changes operation and operationHash. Binding-ID reuse is also an explicit AC-3 obligation.
findings.requiredCorrection: Define authenticated base-revision-to-new-session import for stable input/produced binding IDs and current receipts/proofs, plus suffix collision protection. Alternatively rule canonical recipe identity for hash inputs and recompute operation commitments consistently; cannot simply strip operationHash. Test fresh secret/plain prefix input and binding recapture with same IDs but fresh values/owner/evidence.
findings.owner: Aria identity rule; dev bridge/publication; Dara verify existing session-scoped keys

findings.title: Blind full-base plan/consumer import prevents suffix deletion and drift replacement
findings.observed: acceptPlan requires every prior obligation and need consumer remain; allocations cannot shed consumers. Plans and obligation meanings/admission associations are immutable. Publication requires exact equality of actions, plan obligations and association counts, and all declared consumers exercised.
findings.implication: Importing the full old plan or its suffix graph before replay carries deleted or changed suffix obligations into the new publication and may make a drift switch impossible without replaying old actions.
findings.requiredCorrection: Specify a deterministic prefix obligation seed that preserves actual dispatched identities only, reconstruct current-draft consumers, and append learned suffix under a new plan head. Preserve immutable historical plans and single-assignment associations. Decide how a partially dispatched step j retains completed actions while replanning remaining ordinals. No blanket trigger relaxation.
findings.owner: Aria merge semantics; dev translation/publisher; Dara schema impact review

findings.title: Required replay/switch provenance has no assigned durable home under retention
findings.observed: The pruner retains only stepIndex,errorCode,detail,teardownStatus,publicationRevisionId,publicationRevisionDigest,evidenceRef. baseRevisionId, firstLearnStepId, switch j and prefix checkpoints do not currently exist. New session document fields would not be protected by the V14 explicit immutable-field list. Publication base and publicReceipt have closed SQL key sets.
findings.implication: Storing relearnedFrom only in progress loses the required receipt information after pruning. Adding it to publicReceipt without forward SQL changes fails its deferred shape guard. A mutable session copy of the base pointer is not the immutable publication-base guarantee.
findings.requiredCorrection: Choose an immutable server-resolved session identity for initial base/k and a write-once effective switch/final receipt. Bind base to publication_bases.confirmedRevisionId. Explicitly decide what survives pruning for succeeded and failed runs. If publicReceipt gains keys, update V15 guard via V21; if outer publication/base keys gain keys, replace their CHECKs too. If progress carries retained scalar provenance, extend V19 retained-key function via V21 and regression-test sensitive payload exclusion.
findings.owner: Aria retention/receipt design; C-int shape; Dara forward CHECK/function changes; dev projection

findings.title: Per-step metadata exists only as nullable storage, with no current producer or verifier
findings.observed: Production revision INSERT omits step_snapshot_hashes and step_reuse_provenance. The entity maps neither. Verifier reads artifact/configuration/policy/authoring but neither metadata map nor authoring_revision_inputs/references. Existing metadata test writes synthetic map values explicitly to test DB scope/equality, not production hash composition.
findings.implication: V15 proves capacity and relational constraints, not populated base hashes, readiness computation or prefix provenance. Current published rows have NULL maps through the production path. Existing SQL tests do not satisfy AC-1/AC-5/AC-6.
findings.requiredCorrection: Implement metadata at publication atomically and read/verify it from the immutable revision; define no-metadata base policy before mixed replay. Retain the nullable schema for frozen V15, never retrofit synthesized hashes into immutable rows. Assert full publish and reuse produce real stored maps and verify all values; reject missing/extra/forged maps.
findings.owner: dev publication/readiness/verifier; Dara constraint regression; QA joined oracle

findings.title: Tail deletion is ruled to a real last step; empty suffix is not the adopted representation
findings.observed: T0 maps pure tail deletion to k=draft last step. Empty draft cannot be learned. Optional firstLearnStepId means server chooses, not an end-of-draft sentinel. Installed contracts/code contain no baseRevisionId/firstLearnStepId/REPLAYING_PREFIX implementation.
findings.implication: A draft 1..9 replacing base 1..10 must replay 1..8 and learn 9; it does not have empty learned suffix. New zero-suffix/publish-only semantics would be a change to T0. Deleting all steps can remain a draft but learning is refused.
findings.requiredCorrection: Keep this rule unless Aria explicitly changes it. Add tail-delete to one-step, multi-tail-delete, delete-all refusal, append-after-last and ordinary READY replay tests. If empty suffix is newly required, C3b must define nullable/end sentinel and receipt semantics, and publisher must support it; do not overload an omitted field.
findings.owner: Aria/PO if semantics change; C-int and dev tests

findings.title: Some proposal statements overclaim invariants or misidentify existing guards
findings.observed: The proposal says all Java/terminal lists make the state live everywhere, but runner uses ACTIVE. Its suggested test says only one CHECK names state, but the document.state=state CHECK also names it. V17:515 guards terminal unlinked USAGE, not ordinary secret RELEASE. Excluding replay from runnable without a separate driver stalls it.
findings.implication: These do not invalidate the narrow state CHECK expansion, but would create incorrect test expectations and misleading readiness evidence.
findings.requiredCorrection: Assert exactly one state-vocabulary CHECK plus the unchanged document equality CHECK; preserve unlinked no-decision refusal during prefix and authenticate ordinary RELEASE by existing lineage; enumerate explicit positive ACTIVE lists and document the replay driver.
findings.owner: Dara design update; dev/QA liveness tests

findings.title: Existing reuse guard checks a prior same-scope hash, not immediate pinned-base provenance
findings.observed: The V15 trigger permits a hash-equal GUIDED_RUN revision of the same test/CSI and same step ID. It does not require reusedFrom.revisionId equal this session publication base confirmedRevisionId or require a contiguous actual reused prefix.
findings.implication: Same-scope storage integrity is necessary but does not itself establish AC-5 provenance to the selected base or the drift-switch boundary.
findings.requiredCorrection: Server and verifier must enforce immediate pinned base, exact reused prefix and absence of reusedFrom for j onward. Optionally add a forward DB guard after Aria chooses immutable base/k/switch representation; test same-test wrong-base, suffix mislabeled reused and post-drift reused entries.
findings.owner: dev verifier/publisher; Aria optional DB defense; Dara if ruled
